sentences.text: Last, two unusual craft that Rule eighteen also covers.
A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels and avoid impeding their navigation.
Think of it this way: she can leave by air, so she stays out of the way on the water.
But where risk of collision exists, she follows the steering rules like everyone else.
A wing-in-ground craft, when taking off, landing, or flying near the surface, keeps well clear of all other vessels and avoids impeding their navigation.
And when she’s operating on the water surface, she follows the rules as a power-driven vessel.
The ladder, from the top: broken or busy, then fishing, then sail, then power.
Constrained by draft is International only.
And narrow channels, traffic lanes and overtaking override the ladder.
Next time, we go where none of this applies: into the fog, and Rule nineteen.
